newsitem.title: USA: Microsoft sets tone for tech, Nasdaq decline.
newsitem.headline: Microsoft sets tone for tech, Nasdaq decline.

text.p: Nasdaq shares dropped further on Friday after Microsoft Corp's quarterly earnings, which failed to meet Wall Street's most optimistic expectations, offered a reason to take profits after the recent winning streak, traders said.

The Nasdaq composite index, which had seen a strong rally over the past two weeks until taking a breather on Thursday, slipped further on Friday. The index lost 20.89 points or 1.33 percent to an unofficial close of 1547.96. Declining issues beat gainers 12 to nine on total volume of 674 million shares.
Microsoft, the second most active Nasdaq issue, lost 9 to 140-1/2 after just barely beating analysts' estimates and warning that growth will slow over the coming year.

"Microsoft set the tone for the day. There was bound to be some relaxation after this intense run up. A few smaller companies had some disappointing numbers, so people decided to cash in their chips and call it a week," one trader said.

Micro Linear dropped about 37 percent to 8-1/2 after posting second quarter earnings of $0.19 a share compared to $0.14 a share a year ago on a 43 percent rise in revenues. Synopsys Inc also slipped after its earnings report. Several brokerage firms also downgraded the stock.
